title: Compute deterministic fourth-order first-shell attenuation
statement: For Z(A,B)=[A,[B,[A,B]]]=2ABAB-2BABA-A²B²+B²A²,let D4=(1/4)sum_(distinct i,j,l)sum_(alpha,beta in cos,sin)Z(A_ij^alpha,A_jl^beta). Four phase choices cancel every nonzero net shift,so D4 is an EXACT Fourier multiplier without truncation. Rational transition matrices P_(k+sigma e_j)(k_i I+sigma e_i e_j^T)P_k give D4 P1=-(kappa^4/3)P1 on the ENTIRE real twelve-dimensional first shell,both polarizations. At k=e1+e2,the transverse eigenvalues of D4/kappa^4 are1/45 and8/45,both positive. This is deterministic low-shell amplitude attenuation,not the earlier stochastic covariance operation or global dissipativity.
